raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The LoRA Serving page explains how to start a LoRA server, but it does not explain what makes a PEFT adapter compatible with SGLang's runtime layout. This leaves users without a documented path when an adapter uses a regex `target_modules` string, or when the adapter targets an unfused projection that SGLang fuses at runtime.

This PR adds an "Adapter compatibility" section to `docs/docs/advanced_features/lora.mdx`. It documents the `target_modules` list requirement, common fused-name mappings, the model-specific `supported_lora_modules` contract, when repacking is needed, and a short verification recipe. It does not change runtime behavior.

This is based on a real Qwen3.5-family 27B GDN hybrid MoE adapter exported by PEFT/ms-swift. The adapter uses a regex `target_modules` string and split `in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `in_proj_b`, and `in_proj_a` tensors. This PR turns that compatibility contract into documentation; it does not change runtime behavior.

## Modifications

- `docs/docs/advanced_features/lora.mdx`: add an "Adapter compatibility" section after the LoRA serving arguments.
- Document that `target_modules` must be a list of suffixes. An arbitrary regex string is rejected even when `--lora-target-modules` is provided, because SGLang still validates each adapter's `adapter_config.json`.
- Document the common fused mappings (`q_proj` / `k_proj` / `v_proj` -> `qkv_proj`, `gate_proj` / `up_proj` -> `gate_up_proj`) and the GDN examples (`in_proj_q` / `in_proj_k` / `in_proj_v` / `in_proj_z` -> `in_proj_qkvz`, `in_proj_qkv` + `in_proj_z` -> `in_proj_qkvz`, `in_proj_b` + `in_proj_a` -> `in_proj_ba`), with a note that support is model- and version-specific.
- Clarify that repacking changes module names and tensor layout only, and must preserve `r`, `lora_alpha`, `lora_dropout`, and the A/B values.
- Add a verification checklist: use `--lora-strict-loading`, inspect the resolved target set, confirm the adapter appears in `/v1/models`, and compare base and adapter outputs at temperature 0.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This is a documentation-only change and does not modify model execution.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This is a documentation-only change and does not modify kernels or the serving path.

## Checklist

- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (MDX-only change; no Python formatting changes.)
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Not applicable to a docs-only change.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -38,6 +38,78 @@ The following server arguments are relevant for multi-LoRA serving:
 From client side, the user needs to provide a list of strings as input batch, and a list of adaptor names that each input sequence corresponds to.
 
 
+## Adapter compatibility
+
+SGLang loads PEFT-format adapters without rewriting the adapter files. It normalizes some layouts in memory and resolves each target to a module that the runtime exposes. Before you serve an adapter, check its `adapter_config.json` and the model implementation's `supported_lora_modules` list.
+
+### `target_modules` must be a list
+
+SGLang reads `target_modules` from each adapter config to infer the LoRA target set. Use a list of module-name suffixes:
+
+```json
+{
+  "target_modules": [
+    "q_proj",
+    "k_proj",
+    "v_proj",
+    "o_proj",
+    "gate_proj",
+    "up_proj",
+    "down_proj"
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+The strings `"all"` and `"all-linear"` are also accepted and are resolved against the base model. Arbitrary regular expressions are not accepted. For example, a PEFT config containing a regex such as:
+
+```json
+{
+  "target_modules": "^(model\\.layers\\..*\\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj))$"
+}
+```
+
+fails during LoRA initialization with an error such as:
+
+```text
+SGLang does not recognize target_modules='...'
+```
+
+Older versions may report `Only 'all' or 'all-linear' can be used as the string for target module`. Rewrite the regex as the list of module suffixes it matches. SGLang resolves targets by module name, so a regex that restricts matches to specific layer indices or to one submodule subtree cannot be represented exactly; check the resolved target set before serving.
+
+Passing `--lora-target-modules` does not bypass this check. SGLang still validates each adapter's `target_modules` field and raises before the flag can help.
+
+### Fused target modules
+
+SGLang may fuse projections at runtime. It normalizes some common target names and weight layouts automatically:
+
+| Adapter module names | Runtime target | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj` | `qkv_proj` | Target names and weight keys are normalized automatically. |
+| `gate_proj`, `up_proj` | `gate_up_proj` | Target names and weight keys are normalized automatically. |
+| `in_proj_q`, `in_proj_k`, `in_proj_v`, `in_proj_z` | `in_proj_qkvz` | GDN models only. Weight keys may be packed; set `target_modules` to the fused name if your version does not map the split target names. |
+| `in_proj_qkv` + `in_proj_z` | `in_proj_qkvz` | Two-way GDN weight packing. Target-name support depends on the SGLang version. |
+| `in_proj_b` + `in_proj_a` | `in_proj_ba` | Requires the model to list `in_proj_ba` in `supported_lora_modules`. Do not assume automatic mapping. |
+| `out_proj`, `o_proj`, `down_proj`, `lm_head` | Same name | Check the model support list. |
+
+Target-name normalization and weight-layout normalization are separate steps. A version may pack split weight keys while still not mapping the split names in `target_modules`. If SGLang rejects the adapter's target set, use the fused name that appears in `supported_lora_modules`, or use a version that maps the split names.
+
+Name normalization is necessary but not sufficient. The model class must also expose the module in `supported_lora_modules` and implement its input and output dimensions. If a fused target is absent from that list, the adapter cannot be applied even when its tensor names look correct. Check the model implementation for the SGLang version you run. Starting the server with `--lora-target-modules all` logs the resolved target set and is a quick way to inspect what the current model and version expose.
+
+### Repacking an adapter
+
+If the adapter layout is not supported by your SGLang version, repack the adapter before serving it. Repacking changes module names and tensor layout only. It must preserve `r`, `lora_alpha`, `lora_dropout`, and the values of the A and B matrices. A correct repack is mathematically equivalent to the original adapter.
+
+Do not drop projections merely to make an adapter fit. For example, removing the GDN `b` and `a` deltas changes the model even if the server starts successfully.
+
+### Verify that the adapter is active
+
+1. Start the server with `--lora-paths` and, if needed, `--lora-target-modules`.
+2. Query `/v1/models` and confirm that the adapter name is present.
+3. Start with `--lora-strict-loading` to fail on missing or unexpected adapter keys.
+4. Send the same prompt to the base model and the adapter with `temperature=0`. Use a prompt that exercises the fine-tune. Also compare logprobs, because a small adapter can leave greedy text unchanged.
+5. Check the startup log for the adapter load message and the resolved target modules.
+
+
